title: Vice President Quality Control
text:
**This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Vice President, Quality Control based in the United States.**
The Vice President, Quality Control will provide strategic leadership for a global laboratory network supporting clinical development and commercial manufacturing programs. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, this executive will define and implement an enterprise-wide Quality Control strategy, ensuring scientific excellence, regulatory compliance, reliable data, and timely product release. The role oversees a broad range of laboratory operations across multiple sites and product modalities, while driving standardization, digital transformation, and operational performance. Working closely with senior executives, strategic clients, and regulatory authorities, the successful candidate will influence investment decisions, strengthen inspection readiness, and protect continuity of supply. This is an opportunity to shape a high-performing global organization and make a meaningful contribution to product quality and patient safety.
 
 
Accountabilities
 
 

* Define and execute the global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap across sites, product modalities, and development stages. Establish consistent enterprise standards, governance structures, and decision-making responsibilities while accommodating justified site-specific requirements.
* Provide executive oversight of end-to-end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw-material, in-process, release, and stability testing, as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure laboratory capacity, priorities, and execution support program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure testing strategies and specifications evolve appropriately throughout clinical development, process performance qualification, product launch, and commercial supply.
* Establish global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance and integrity, laboratory investigations, out-of-specification and out-of-trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise-level regulatory inspection strategies and responses to critical client audits.
* Drive the global laboratory digital and technology roadmap, including laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated technology deployment, master-data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption to improve accuracy, efficiency, and cycle times.
* Lead enterprise capacity planning, capital investment prioritization, make-versus-buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and oversight of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resilience requirements.
* Establish enterprise performance metrics and management reviews covering testing and release timelines, lead times, invalid results, out-of-specification and out-of-trend rates, investigation cycle times, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Promote risk-based decision-making, Lean practices, and cross-site learning.
* Act as the senior Quality Control representative for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex technical and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate scientifically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic and consistently delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Develop organizational capabilities, succession plans, technical career paths, and communities of practice while fostering scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Lead escalations and coordinated responses to significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, data-integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk-based decisions regarding testing strategies, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform additional responsibilities in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and organizational objectives.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with at least 15 years of progressive Quality Control experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) sector; alternatively, a Master's degree with at least 10 years of relevant experience.
* At least 10 years of people-management experience, including a minimum of five years leading senior leaders with responsibility for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control operations across clinical development and commercial manufacturing, including analytical method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience managing global regulatory inspections and client audits, as well as complex out-of-specification, out-of-trend, data-integrity, and laboratory-compliance matters.
* Experience overseeing budgets, capital investment portfolios, headcount, laboratory capacity, external testing partners, and enterprise transformation initiatives within a complex, matrixed global organization.
* Strong executive communication, stakeholder-management, and client-facing skills, with the ability to communicate complex scientific and regulatory matters clearly and influence strategic decisions.
* An advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration is preferred.
* Global leadership experience within a CDMO supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing is highly desirable.
* Experience scaling Quality Control capabilities from clinical development through process performance qualification, product launch, and sustained commercial supply is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of relevant regulatory authorities, standards, and guidance, including the US Food and Drug Administration, European Medicines Agency, Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, and Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency.
* Familiarity with International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; and applicable data-integrity expectations.
* Experience implementing global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation initiatives is preferred.
* Professional credentials from the American Society for Quality, along with Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent quality and operational excellence training, are valued.

**Benefits**

* Annual salary range of $272,000–$325,000, with compensation determined by work location and relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.
* Medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.
* Health Savings Account option with company contributions.
* Industry-leading 401(k) savings plan.
* Insurance coverage and employee assistance programs.
* Wellness incentives designed to support overall health and well-being.
* Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays.
* A supportive environment that encourages personal and professional development.
* Global scope, with the role supporting sites worldwide. Compensation and benefits are governed by the location designated as the employee's home site.
